name: Transcribe Spanish Script (19th-20th C., Multi-Pass)
description: Three-step transcription preset for 19th-20th century Spanish notarial and secretarial handwriting. Pass 1 drafts from the page image, Pass 2 performs a lightweight review against the image plus reference hits, and Pass 3 performs a stronger final reconciliation that updates page content. All three vision passes intentionally defer to the user's configured vision defaults and paid-fallback policy instead of pinning provider aliases inside the preset.

config.prompt:
You are transcribing Spanish Script (19th-20th c.) from a manuscript image. This page is from Spanish notarial or secretarial cursive, not early-modern paleography. Produce a draft transcription for later review.

Context:
- Expect 19th-20th century Spanish script, including notarial and administrative formulas.
- Treat unusual spellings, abbreviations, names, dates, and money amounts as documentary evidence, not mistakes.
- The goal is faithful capture, not modernisation.

Rules:
- Output ONLY the transcription. No commentary, no summary, no preamble, no script analysis.
- Preserve original orthography exactly as written, including i/j/y usage, accenting, punctuation, abbreviations, honorifics, and formulaic legal phrasing.
- Preserve names, place names, dates, money, folio markers, and line breaks exactly as visible.
- Include all visible text elements: headings, body text, marginalia, stamps, signatures, and inserted words.
- Keep crossed-out text as [deleted: <text>].
- Keep uncertain readings inline as [UNCERTAIN]. Use [ILLEGIBLE] only when text is truly unreadable.
- Do not hallucinate or silently complete unreadable text.
- If a line or word is unreadable, leave the uncertainty marker at that exact position.
- If the image has no legible text, output [sin texto].

You are reviewing a draft transcription against the original image for Spanish Script (19th-20th c.), especially Spanish notarial and secretarial cursive.

The draft appears in the Context section above. Compare it directly against the image and against any reference snippets provided in metadata.

Review priorities:
- Preserve original orthography exactly as written; do not modernise spelling or punctuation.
- Verify names, dates, money amounts, abbreviations, and honorific formulas character by character.
- Keep original line breaks and paragraph breaks.
- Check for skipped marginalia, stamps, signatures, inserted words, and crossed-out text.
- Use [UNCERTAIN] for plausible low-confidence readings and [ILLEGIBLE] for truly unreadable text.
- Do not hallucinate or silently expand unreadable spans.

Rules:
- Output ONLY the corrected transcription. No commentary, no diff, no preamble.
- If the draft is already correct, return it verbatim.
- Preserve [deleted: ...] markers where applicable.

You are performing the final reconciliation pass for a Spanish Script (19th-20th c.) transcription from a manuscript image. The prior reviewed draft appears in the Context section above.

This is the final pass before saving page content. Re-check the image carefully and produce the best faithful transcription you can without inventing text.

Final-pass priorities:
- Preserve original orthography exactly as written. Do not modernise spellings, grammar, abbreviations, or punctuation.
- Preserve names, place names, dates, money amounts, legal formulas, signatures, stamps, and line breaks exactly as visible.
- Resolve draft mistakes where the image is clear, but keep [UNCERTAIN] or [ILLEGIBLE] when the page does not support a confident reading.
- Never hallucinate missing text, even if the formula seems predictable.
- Keep crossed-out text as [deleted: <text>] and retain inserted words at their visual insertion point.

Rules:
- Output ONLY the corrected final transcription. No commentary, no rationale, no preamble.
- If the prior review is already correct, return it verbatim.
- Update only from what is visibly present in the image and supplied context.
